summary: Gyoko Iotani studied at Rissho University, where he served as an assistant professor (~1983–1993), professor (~1993–2019), and professor emeritus (~2019). He also held a post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Gyokusen Hosaka studied at Komazawa University and served as president of Komazawa Junior College from ~1950 to 1963.
Gyomay Kubose worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under Haya Akegarasu from ~1937 to 1941.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Gyoon Iotani studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and served as deputy director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyosho Takahashi worked in Buddhist studies, holding professorships at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).
Gyoshu Nakajo specialized in Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and a professor in the Faculty of Buddhism at Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged (1928–1934) and held a post at Nyugat from ~1933 to 1940.

A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, Gyurme Dorje studied at Edinburgh and under Philip Denwood at SOAS. He held a fellowship at London (~1991–1996) and worked as a translator at the Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
Gyurme Wosel studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

György Kara studied at Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University. He served as director at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1975–2000) and professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1993–2022).
Working in Indology and religious studies, Gérard Colas held posts as research director at the CNRS and at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.

Gérard Fussman, working in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics, studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1960–1964) and became a professor at the Collège de France in 1984, succeeding Jean Filliozat.
A scholar of computational linguistics and Indology, Gérard Huet studied under George Ernst and Maurice Nivat. He served as a professor at Inria from ~1974 to 2014.

Géza Bethlenfalvy studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Lajos Ligeti. Working in Tibetology and Indology, he held posts at the University of Delhi (1970), Eötvös Loránd University (~1986–2006), and the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

Gösta Liebert studied at Lund and Gothenburg universities. Specializing in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Lund University (1950), Uppsala University (1951–1953), and served as professor at the University of Gothenburg from 1955 to 1982.

Götz von Selle studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen. He served at the Göttingen State and University Library, Prussian State Library, University of Göttingen, and as professor and library deputy director at the University of Königsberg (~1938–1945).
Specializing in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Günter Grönbold served at the Bavarian State Library from ~1974 to 2008, where he headed the Oriental Section from ~1987 to 2008.

Günter Schweiger studied under Gert Klingenschmitt and at Vienna University of Economics and Business, where he later served as full professor from 1974 to 2009 after an assistantship at Johannes Kepler University Linz (~1966–1972).

Linguist H. Craig Melchert studied at Michigan State University and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2007–2015).

Indologist H. G. Narahari studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras under Chittenjoor Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he was attested as a research assistant at Adyar Library and research fellow at Madras.
